title: Video Streaming Service: Complete Architecture
description: Design a video streaming service with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a video-on-demand and live streaming platform that accepts uploads from creators, transcodes videos into multiple bitrates and resolutions (HLS and DASH), stores content durably, and streams to millions of viewers with adaptive bitrate selection. The system must generate thumbnails, ingest closed captions, enforce DRM for premium content, and serve playback events for analytics.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Upload raw video files up to 10 GB with resumable multipart transfer
Transcode uploads into HLS and DASH renditions at 480p, 720p, 1080p, and 4K
Generate and cache thumbnail images at multiple timestamps
Serve adaptive bitrate streams with automatic quality switching based on bandwidth
Support live streaming with low latency (HLS LL or WebRTC ingest)
Ingest and burn closed captions (WebVTT and SRT) into video renditions
Apply DRM for premium content using Widevine and FairPlay
Track watch history, watch percentage, and playback errors for analytics
Enable search across titles, descriptions, and auto-generated transcripts

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: 99.9% availability for playback endpoints; uploads tolerate intermittent drops
Sub-500ms HLS manifest delivery from edge cache
Transcode 1-hour 1080p video within 15 minutes of upload
Store petabytes of video and images with 99.999999999% durability
Scale to 1 million concurrent viewers per popular title
Support 10,000 simultaneous live streams
End-to-end encryption for premium content in transit and at rest
Analytics pipeline processes playback events in under 60 seconds

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application that handles upload, metadata storage, transcoding job orchestration, and video serving. Use Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for raw and processed video files. The monolith keeps the content pipeline simple while you validate encoding profiles and streaming URLs.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - Minimal API or MVC Controllers
  - Entity Framework Core for data access
  - Azure SQL Database or AWS RDS for relational data
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service or AWS EC2/ECS
  - Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for file assets
  - Azure Monitor or AWS CloudWatch for logging
  - Single database with tables for all domains

data.text: When upload volume and concurrent viewership grow, split into microservices. Upload Service handles multipart uploads and generates presigned URLs. Transcoding Service consumes jobs from a queue and runs FFmpeg in isolated containers or serverless functions. Streaming Service serves HLS playlists and video segments from a CDN with DRM license enforcement. Metadata Service manages titles, descriptions, and search. Media Service owns the media library and watch history.

items: Upload Service: Accepts resumable multipart uploads, generates presigned URLs, validates file size and format, and emits TranscodeJob events to the queue.
Transcoding Service: Consumes transcode jobs, runs FFmpeg to produce HLS and DASH renditions, and stores segments and manifests in blob storage.
Streaming Service: Generates signed playback URLs, enforces DRM licenses (Widevine, FairPlay), serves HLS playlists, and emits watch events.
Metadata Service: Manages video metadata, titles, descriptions, tags, categories, and watch history. Powers search and recommendations.
Thumbnail Service: Extracts frames from videos at configured timestamps, generates sprite sheets for previews, and stores images in blob storage.

    VideoStreamingHld/
      api/           # API clients per service
      components/     # Shared UI components
      hooks/          # Custom hooks
      pages/          # Route pages
      store/          # Zustand/Jotai state
      types/          # TypeScript interfaces
  shared/
    ui/              # Design system
    lib/              # Utilities
    hooks/            # Global hooks

Key Patterns:
  - Feature-based folder structure
  - API Gateway as single entry point
  - React Query for caching and background refetch
  - WebSocket / SSE for real-time updates
  - Error boundaries and retry logic

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: A Video Streaming Service system requires both simple and scalable designs
Monolith is fastest to validate; microservices are for scale
React + ASP.NET Core provides a robust full-stack foundation
Azure Cosmos DB and Amazon DynamoDB are strong choices for distributed data
Always design for failure: retries, circuit breakers, and fallbacks
data.takeaway: Video Streaming Service is a distributed system. Start simple, then scale horizontally with microservices, caching, and managed cloud services.
